stories.title: India crush Pakistan at T20 Asia Cup with record-breaking bowling display
stories.summary: India claim seven-wicket win after Pakistan lose 10 wickets for just 28 runs as they are bowled out for 55. India produced a dominant display to defeat Pakistan by seven wickets in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup in Dubai, bowling their rivals out for their lowest total in the format before rattling off their target inside nine overs. Pakistan, having won the toss and elected to bat at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday, made a promising start but collapsed spectacularly after an opening partnership of 27. India eventually dismissed them for just 55 in 18.1 overs, with their spinners responsible for much of the damage. Shree Charani and Prema Rawat were the stars of the bowling attack, taking three wickets apiece. Charani finished with remarkable figures of 3 for 7 from four overs, while Rawat returned 3 for 9. Deepti Sharma added two wickets for only five runs. Pakistan’s innings initially appeared under control. Muneeba Ali made 13, and Shawaal Zulfiqar scored 14 for the first wicket. But Shafali Verma broke the partnership by bowling Muneeba, and Charani then struck twice in the sixth over. She dismissed Gull Feroza for a duck before removing Zulfiqar, leaving Pakistan 29 for three. The collapse continued almost immediately as Pakistan slipped to 32 for four in the eighth over before Rawat and Deepti Sharma intensified the pressure.

stories.title: Request for pausing strikes on Kiev came through official channels — Putin
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin stated it at a meeting with American negotiators in the Kremlin
article_sentences: The request for pausing strikes on the Ukrainian capital was received by Moscow through official channels, President Vladimir Putin stated at a meeting with American negotiators in the Kremlin.
"We received this request [for ceasing strikes on Kiev] through official channels, through the intelligence services, and through the Foreign Ministry," Putin stated.

stories.title: Putin says Ukraine has significantly reduced number of attacks on Russia
article_sentences: The Ukrainian forces have significantly reduced the number of strikes on Russia, President Vladimir Putin announced at a meeting with American negotiators in the Kremlin.
"I would like to note that the Ukrainian side has also significantly reduced its strikes on the territory of Russia, including on Moscow," Putin stated.
